rationale:
bugs_open/283, round 4 — the canary's finding. The first live conversion (tool-css-unit-converter, item 38efde3b) converted its template EXACTLY to prediction (12 ids / 11 getElementById / 6 id-ref attrs / 5 data-target), the fixer raised its rerender, a 111-page fan-out completed, the page DEPLOYED — and the served page still carried the OLD ids.

THE MECHANISM, read at the config rather than guessed: page-rerender's check_rerender_mode routes to the sections re-render (rerender_page_sections — the path that renders from html_template) ONLY for reasons image_landed | section_data_resolved | cta_links_stale; every other item takes render_page, which ASSEMBLES STORED page_components.rendered_html. 'The component's template changed' had no reason in the vocabulary at all, so every template fix — this lane's 91-row programme included, but also repair_template_slots and chrome fixes before it — ships stale stored HTML under a green status. This is CLC-002's own recorded history repeating: its needs_rerender 'carried no reason, making the triggered re-render assemble-only and unable to repair anything'.

TWO CONFIG CHANGES, applied as migrations 460+461 (snapshot-first via snapshot_agent(), verbatim pre-image guards, DO/RAISE verify induced before trusting):

1. page-rerender.check_rerender_mode gains OR reason=='template_changed'. Additive: the three live reasons and the else-branch are byte-unchanged, so no currently-flowing item changes behaviour. Under the 2026-07-29 owner ruling this is a vocabulary addition that changes no guarantee — the sections path already exists for three causes; this names a fourth.

2. component-template-fixer.create_rerender REPLACED: instead of one site-wide reason-less needs_rerender (111-page fan-out, zero template propagation), it files one page_rerender PER PAGE CARRYING THE FIXED COMPONENT, spec.reason='template_changed', across every site the component is placed on — site_id taken from the PAGE, not the triggering item, which covers RFC_034 §1's cross-domain row. Spec shape copied from the live fan-out items; dedup by NOT EXISTS on an open template_changed item for the same page.

461 exists because 460 embedded a column that does not exist (p.filename) INSIDE the query string — DATA to 460's UPDATE, invisible to its probe run, SQL only when the fixer's query_database step executes. Caught minutes later when the same query shape ran directly. Measured before fixing: nothing in page-rerender reads spec.filename (Go derives it from the page row via PageDeployFilename), so the key is DROPPED, not derived — and 461's verify adds the check 460 lacked: PREPARE-compile the embedded query at apply time.

Proven end-to-end before this submission: with 460+461 live, item 82265e18 (reason=template_changed) was filed for the canary page — the watcher confirms whether the sections path fires and the served page flips; the submission does not claim that result, only the config now routes it.

plan.summary: Add 'template_changed' to page-rerender's reason vocabulary and make component-template-fixer file page-scoped rerenders carrying it, so a template fix actually reaches served pages. Config-only (agent_definitions), applied as guarded migrations 460+461; no Go change, no new registry keys.

edits.rationale: The vocabulary gap is the root cause; the fixer's reason-less site-wide item is the propagation half. Both guarded on verbatim pre-images so a concurrent session's edit aborts the file rather than being reverted.

460's inner query referenced pages.filename, which does not exist; the column is derived in Go and nothing reads spec.filename. 461 drops the key and adds the missing check class: PREPARE-compile the embedded query in the verify block, so an unparseable inner query can never survive apply again.
edits.sketch:
UPDATE ... SET query = replace(query, ',''filename'',p.filename', '') WHERE <post-image of 460 guard: query LIKE '%p.filename%'>;
DO $$ ... IF q LIKE '%filename%' THEN RAISE; EXECUTE 'PREPARE chk461 AS ' || q; DEALLOCATE chk461; $$;

grounded_in: Live config read 2026-08-18: check_rerender_mode condition was exactly "input_data.spec.reason == 'image_landed' OR ... 'section_data_resolved' OR ... 'cta_links_stale'" with else_step render_page (assemble stored HTML).

Measured end-to-end on the canary: item 38efde3b fixed:true with every predicted count; needs_rerender completed; batch 486e96c9 = 111/111 page_rerender complete including 'Rerender page: tool-css-unit-converter' (whose result shows a successful DEPLOY of tools/css-unit-converter/index.html); page_components.rendered_html unchanged (updated_at 2026-08-15) and the served page greps 1 for id="input-value", 0 for c-tool-css-unit-converter.

CLC-002 (concept register): the needs_rerender reason mechanism exists precisely because a reason-less item 'made the triggered re-render assemble-only and unable to repair anything' — this gap is that entry's recorded history repeating on a new writer.
rerender_single_page_action.go: assemblePage assembles from stored components; loadVerbatimPageHTML/verbatim path not involved (canary page rebuild_policy='generic', no deploy_mode).

Measured before 461: information_schema.columns for pages has no filename; PageDeployFilename(url, name) derives it in Go (rerender_pages_actions.go:324, rerender_single_page_action.go:554); zero occurrences of 'spec.filename' in page-rerender's workflow steps.

Both migrations probe-run before apply (460 with COMMIT->ROLLBACK; verify DO/RAISE induced against unchanged rows and it RAISEd); 461's PREPARE check compiled the corrected query at apply time. Snapshots exist in agent_definitions_backup (reasons '460 pre-image…', '461 pre-image…').
plan.risks:
1. The new reason routes an item class onto rerender_page_sections that previously took assembly. That path is LLM-free and record-only on collisions, but it recomputes resolved fields; a page whose stored content_data disagrees with fresh resolution will change beyond the template fix. This is the same exposure the three existing reasons already carry.
2. The fixer now fans out per PAGE per component instead of one site item — for the 3 multi-page rows that is 2 items instead of 1; bounded by placements, and deduped.
3. Config is live immediately; the Go binary is untouched. If the sections path mis-renders a page class the remedy is removing the reason from the conditional (one guarded UPDATE, snapshots exist).
4. The 111-page fan-out shape (site-wide assemble+deploy for a reason-less needs_rerender) is UNCHANGED for every other producer — this round narrows only the template-fix path. Whether reason-less site-wide rerenders should exist at all is a bigger question, deliberately not smuggled in here.
